content.value_statement: Python code can drift into mutable models, vague types, and weak error handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward typed models, clearer failures, and structured logging.
actual_capabilities: Promotes frozen dataclasses for immutable domain models.
Shows discriminated unions with Literal for explicit request states.
Uses NewType examples for safer domain identifiers.
Defines Protocol patterns for structural typing.
Recommends exception chaining with from err.
Suggests structured logging with deferred formatting.
limitations: Provides guidance only. It does not run type checkers by itself.
Focuses on language idioms, not full application architecture.
Mentions ty, pyright, and mypy without full configuration coverage.
Examples may need adaptation for existing codebases.

use_cases.title: Review Python Domain Models
use_cases.description: Check models for mutability, vague identifiers, and missing type boundaries before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve Service Error Handling
use_cases.description: Refine exception paths so failures preserve context and remain easy to diagnose.

use_cases.title: Prepare Type Checking Guidance
use_cases.description: Choose practical typing patterns and type checker options for a Python project.

prompt_templates.title: Improve A Python File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python file with the python-best-practices skill. Suggest focused improvements for types, immutability, errors, and logging.

prompt_templates.title: Add Safer Domain Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this module to replace plain identifiers with safer domain types. Keep the public behavior unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Errors And Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this service layer with clearer exception chaining and structured logging. Preserve existing tests unless they are wrong.

prompt_templates.title: Design Typed Workflow States
prompt_templates.prompt: Design request state models for this workflow using typed variants. Explain how each state prevents invalid transitions.

output_examples.input: A service passes plain strings for user and order identifiers.
output: Replace broad string identifiers with domain-specific types.
Keep function signatures aligned with those types.
Add tests that catch swapped identifiers.

output_examples.input: A parser catches an error and raises a generic failure.
output: Preserve the original exception as the cause.
Use a clear message that names the failed payload type.
Log useful context without exposing sensitive data.

output_examples.input: A workflow stores status as a free-form string.
output: Model each valid state as a named variant.
Move state-specific fields into the matching variant.
Use exhaustive handling to prevent missing cases.

best_practices: Use immutable domain models when values should not change after creation.
Make state choices explicit with typed variants.
Log structured context without formatting messages early.
anti_patterns: Passing many plain strings where domain-specific identifiers are safer.
Swallowing original exceptions and losing traceback context.
Using print statements instead of module-level structured logging.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Optional type checker examples should require user approval before execution.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it replace a linter?
faq.answer: No. Use it with linters, formatters, and type checkers.

faq.question: Which Python versions fit best?
faq.answer: Examples use modern Python features such as union types and pattern matching. Python 3.10 or newer is the best fit.

faq.question: Does it cover packaging?
faq.answer: Only lightly. It focuses on Python language patterns, error handling, typing, and logging.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide targeted reviews and refactors when source files are provided.
